defectsFoundThisSession.summary: T-SQL ROUND rounds half away from zero; .NET Math.Round uses banker's rounding. An observed 0.325 is 33% on the server and 32% in .NET.

Fifteen engines are built and explainable; nothing is deployed, there are no backups, there is no monitoring, and the mobile client has never been executed. Two things are worth more than the planner and neither is engine work: (1) deploy something with backups and a rehearsed restore — the database is in SIMPLE recovery with zero rows in backupset; (2) answer PD-1 and the tenancy question while the Health domain is still nine tables and zero procedures, because tenancy stops being a design choice the moment that procedure layer is written. The planner is the right next engine; whether the next engine is the right next thing is a question for a person.

architecturalInvariants: Predict.fn_PredictFrom is the ONLY framing logic, and it cannot compute. A PredictionType carries a SourceFamily pinned to 'probability' by a CHECK, and (SourceMeasureCode, SourceFamily) is a foreign key into Behaviour.MeasureType (MeasureCode, Family) — so a prediction may only name a measure Behaviour publishes as a probability. A CHECK refuses a framing missing {chance}, {window} or {support}, so no configuration can state a likelihood without its window and its support.

Coach.fn_ExplainFrom is the ONLY explanation logic. A message is filled into a tone pattern; a CHECK constraint refuses a pattern missing {body} or {reason}, so no configuration can encourage without evidence. The coach never reassembles.
Recommend.fn_AssembleFrom is the ONLY assembly logic. It consumes an EvidenceSet and reads no raw store — verified by dependency graph. The live path and the Decision Inspector both feed it.

Behaviour.fn_Measure is the ONLY copy of the measure arithmetic. It consumes a DaySet and an HourSet and reads no per-user source — verified by dependency graph, not by text. The real observer and the Decision Inspector both feed it.
Behaviour.fn_Observe is the only computation of behaviour. Consumption goes through Behaviour.fn_Read and Behaviour.fn_ReadSteps.
Growth.Routine NEVER owns a step list. It references Behaviour.Subject. Asserted structurally: no Step/EventType/Percent column may exist on Growth.Routine.
Routine completion is derived from logged events every time. No stored percentage, no mark-complete command, no completion endpoint. Asserted at the contract boundary too.
Goal achievement is earned from the timeline, forward-only, and refused to clients by validator and procedure.
Applicability for content, dashboard cards, goals and routines all go through Rules.fn_Match. One matcher.

Reminder timing is deliberately NOT a prediction. Behaviour already observes preferred_hour; restating an observation in the future tense would be a rename, and the foreign key above cannot express it because a preference is not a probability.
